research.angle: While online networks can create filter bubbles and polarized communities around conspiracy news, experimental evidence suggests that social information exchange in homogeneous networks can actually improve accuracy and reduce polarization.
research.verdict: The evidence contradicts the proposed angle by showing that social interaction in networks can improve collective intelligence and reduce bias, even if platform algorithms and specific content types contribute to polarization.
research.caveat: The studies differ in their findings because some focus on the structural dynamics of content recommendation (filter bubbles) while others measure the outcomes of active social information exchange.
